result.summary: Rework 02c (decisions/0137 Addition 5) on bddef13: app/server/db/pg.js transaction() now attaches an `error` listener to the client it checks out, for the whole time it is held. After the event every further statement fails as DbError E_DB_DOWN, which the pipeline answers 503 db_unavailable and logs with the code only. The client is released as broken (release(true)), so the pool drops it. A client returned to the pool normally loses the listener (the pool's idle listener takes over); a dropped client keeps it while it ends. index.js is unchanged. The design has one row in section 7 and one line in section 19. No test file was edited.

changes.text: transaction(): `broken` flag and a client `error` listener added after pool.connect(); run() throws DbError E_DB_DOWN once broken; release(drop) calls client.release(drop || broken) and removes the listener only when the client goes back to the pool; the catch path (the ROLLBACK, not awaited) and the commit path use release(); DbError imported.
section 7: one row «A database connection drops while a request transaction holds it»; section 19: table «Rework 02c» with one line (the change and the ADD-4 test line).

self_check: probe p9-drop on the copy under <scratch> (a plain script, not node --test). The ADD-4 logic uses the fixture pgStandIn (stalls after the start) and a TCP relay cut while the transaction's statement is held, two rounds. Before the fix: each round answered DbError E_DB_DOWN but raised an uncaught «Error: Connection terminated unexpectedly» (2 in all). After the fix: each round DbError E_DB_DOWN at 173-175 ms with no uncaught error.

Other paths, same probe, against an answering stand-in: the commit path commits (begin, select 1, commit); a throw of fn rejects with the same error object and sends rollback; a plain query afterwards answers; no uncaught error at the end.
npx prettier --check, npx eslint --max-warnings 0 and npx tsc --noEmit -p jsconfig.json on app/server/db/pg.js → exit 0 each.
cd tools && npm run -s traces → 0 traces; cd tools && npm run -s handoffs-check → exit 0 (after this result).

issues.text: Only an E_DB_DOWN reaches the caller: the pg error message (it may name the host and port) is never kept, as before (toDbError), so the log line of the request holds the code db_unavailable only. No other pg.js path changed; the pool-level listener for idle clients (pool.on("error")) stays as it was.
